summary: NV2A_VK_BLEND_PAD_ALPHA is declared as 0x00030000, 'synthetic, bits 16..17', on the stated ground that 'NV_PGRAPH_BLEND defines bits 0..11'. It does not. nv2a_regs.h:413 defines NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP_ENABLE as (1 << 16) and nv2a_regs.h:414 defines NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP as 0x0000F000 -- so the register's defined fields run to bit 16, and the synthetic field's LOW BIT IS THE GUEST'S COLOUR-LOGIC-OP ENABLE. init_pipeline_key() then strips exactly that bit at draw.c:1827, `key->regs[0] &= ~(NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP_ENABLE | NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP)`, which runs AFTER key->regs[0] is assigned the effective register at draw.c:1815. PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ZERO is 1, so it lives entirely in bit 16 and is erased; PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE is 0. The two are therefore INDISTINGUISHABLE in the pipeline cache key, for both _Z formats -- which is precisely the aliasing the synthetic field was added to prevent.
scenario: A device where r->eds3_blend_supported is false, so key->regs[0] is not zeroed at draw.c:1833 and blend state is baked into the pipeline. `Blend surface` renders all 32 cases into ONE 128x128 surface at one address, changing only NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT; A8R8G8B8 and X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 share B8G8R8A8_UNORM, so the render-pass state (init_render_pass_state, draw.c:1312, host vk_format only) is identical and every other key register is identical. The pad field is the only thing that differs -- and after line 1827 it does not differ, because ZERO and NONE both key as 0. The cache serves one pipeline to both. In the direction NONE-pipeline -> ZERO-draw the shader stamps (the uniform is staged per draw, psh.c:3772) while the colour blend still names VK_BLEND_FACTOR_SRC_ALPHA, which now reads index 0's stamped constant: that is arm 1's measured defect verbatim, the eight Blend_surface/*_Add_SrcA_* captures, four of them from bit-exact. In the direction ZERO-pipeline -> NONE-draw an A8R8G8B8 draw inherits the forced ONE/ZERO/ADD alpha equation and loses the guest's alpha blend on a format whose alpha channel is real data. The _O formats are unaffected (PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ONE is 2, bit 17, which survives the mask) -- so the bug is silent on exactly half the pad formats, which is the shape that makes it survive a partial reading of a score table.
remediation: Move the synthetic field out of the low bits of NV_PGRAPH_BLEND's defined range -- bits 20..21 (0x00300000) are clear of both LOGICOP_ENABLE and LOGICOP -- or, better, stop riding the register: the field's stated job is to enter three cache keys, and a separate scalar compared alongside key->regs[0], r->dyn_state.blend and e->dyn_blend does that without aliasing a hardware field. Whichever is chosen, add the assertion the current comment substitutes for: a compile-time check that the synthetic mask does not intersect any NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_* field, so the next field added to that register cannot silently re-collide. Do NOT simply widen the mask at line 1827 -- that leaves the H2 direction live. NOTE FOR PASS 2: H1 and H2 are the same collision seen from two sides and one relocation fixes both, but they must be verified separately, because a fix that only reorders the mask at 1827 closes H1 and not H2.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/nv2a_regs.h:363-414 -- the full NV_PGRAPH_BLEND field list, ending LOGICOP (0x0000F000, bits 12-15) and LOGICOP_ENABLE ((1 << 16)). draw.c:572 (the #define, and the comment claiming bits 0..11). draw.c:1815 (key->regs[0] = pgraph_vk_effective_blend_reg(pg)) then draw.c:1827-1828 (the strip, inside `#if OPT_DYNAMIC_STATES` but OUTSIDE `if (use_dyn_ds)`, so it runs on every device where that option is compiled in). draw.c:1832-1838 (regs[0] zeroed only when eds3_blend_supported). psh.h:145-149 (PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE=0, ZERO=1, ONE=2). draw.c:1312-1317 (render-pass state is host format only). draw.c:2203-2250 (the static path bakes the factors and applies the pad substitution). Not build-verified: the desktop build is a KNOWN NAMED GAP on this host, libcurl4-openssl-dev is not installed.

summary: The same bit-16 collision, read the other way. pgraph_vk_effective_blend_reg() writes the pad field ONLY when pgraph_glsl_dual_src_pad_supported() is true (draw.c:578). When it is false the SET_MASK is skipped and bits 16..17 keep whatever the raw register holds -- and bit 16 is NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP_ENABLE, which the guest sets through NV097_SET_LOGIC_OP_ENABLE (pgraph.c:3951-3955). pgraph_vk_blend_stamps_pad_alpha() reads GET_MASK(reg, 0x00030000) and compares against PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE, so a guest that enables a colour logic op makes that predicate return TRUE on a device with NO dual-source blending. pgraph_vk_reg_r() does not mask the register (vk/renderer.h:1490-1497; the dynamic-mask table gates generation counters inside pgraph_reg_w only, pgraph.h:458-478), so the bit reaches the predicate unaltered. This is the feature-absent path the audit was commissioned for, and it fails: absence of dualSrcBlend is supposed to be a refusal to enable, and here the guest can turn the write side on anyway.
scenario: A device without dualSrcBlend, or with the feature and maxFragmentDualSrcAttachments == 0 -- so instance.c leaves the gate false, psh.c declares no index-1 output and emits no `fragColorSrc1`, and the shader has ONE fragment output. The guest issues NV097_SET_LOGIC_OP_ENABLE with a non-zero parameter, which real Xbox titles do (D3DRS_LOGICOP), and then any blended draw. pgraph_vk_blend_stamps_pad_alpha() is true, so: on the static path create_pipeline (draw.c:2245-2256) rewrites SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA to VK_BLEND_FACTOR_SRC1_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC1_ALPHA with dualSrcBlend disabled, violating VUID-VkPipelineColorBlendAttachmentState-srcColorBlendFactor-00608/-00609, and vkCreateGraphicsPipelines is called under VK_CHECK at draw.c:1702 -- an abort, not a degraded picture. On the eds3 path (draw.c:4494-4503) the same factors go to vkCmdSetColorBlendEquationEXT, which is undefined without the feature and a hard validation error under the validation layers. And independently of the factor substitution, the forced srcAlpha=ONE/dstAlpha=ZERO/ADD fires on EVERY logic-op-enabled blended draw, destroying the guest's alpha blend on formats with a real alpha channel. No arm on this fleet could have reached any of this: the Adreno part advertises the feature, so the gate is true there and SET_MASK overwrites bit 16 before the predicate ever sees it.
remediation: Same relocation as H1: take the field out of NV_PGRAPH_BLEND's defined bits, or off the register entirely. Then, so the feature-absent path is guarded by construction rather than by the field happening to be clear, make pgraph_vk_blend_stamps_pad_alpha() itself return false when pgraph_glsl_dual_src_pad_supported() is false -- one condition read at the point of use, which is cheap and is the check the three call sites currently lack. That second half is NOT redundant with the relocation: it is what makes the no-dual-source path safe against any future writer of those bits, and it is the difference between 'nothing sets the field today' and 'nothing can act on the field'.
evidence: draw.c:574-584 (SET_MASK gated on the device feature), draw.c:586-590 (the predicate, ungated). hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/pgraph.c:3951-3955 (DEF_METHOD(NV097, SET_LOGIC_OP_ENABLE) writes bit 16 via PG_SET_MASK). vk/renderer.h:1490-1497 (pgraph_vk_reg_r returns the register unmasked). pgraph.h:458-478 (the dynamic mask affects only the generation counters). draw.c:1702 (VK_CHECK on vkCreateGraphicsPipelines). draw.c:2245, 4494, 5940 (the three substitution sites). instance.c:987-1009 (the gate that is supposed to make this unreachable). A grep for LOGICOP across hw/xbox/nv2a/ returns pgraph.c:72,324,3954,3960 and draw.c:1733-1734 only -- the vk renderer implements no logic op, which is why the clobber in the OTHER direction (gate true, non-pad format, bit 16 zeroed in the effective value) is currently inert; it is the same defect and should not be left resting on that.

summary: The synthetic field reaches the pipeline KEY but not the pipeline DECISION. create_pipeline() early-returns at draw.c:1869-1881 without calling init_pipeline_key() at all when pipeline_state_gen, shader_state_gen, the texture gens and check_render_pass_dirty() are all unchanged. A colour-format-only change moves none of them: pg->surface_shape.color_format is a plain PGRAPHState field, not a pgraph register, so pgraph_reg_w()'s generation machinery never runs for it, and DEF_METHOD(NV097, SET_SURFACE_FORMAT) bumps shader_state_gen/non_dynamic_reg_gen/any_reg_gen ONLY when the ZETA format changes (pgraph.c:2467-2474). Nothing bumps pipeline_state_gen. bind_surface() sets r->pipeline_state_dirty (surface.c:1826) but is not reached when the wanted binding is already the bound one, which is the whole `Blend surface` case. So on the static pipeline path the previous case's blend state is served, and the key that would have caught it is never built.
scenario: A device where r->eds3_blend_supported is false. Draw into X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 at address A; NV097_SET_SURFACE_FORMAT to A8R8G8B8 at the same address, pitch and size, so check_surface_compatibility() reuses the binding and no rebind occurs; draw again. create_pipeline() takes the early return, the pipeline from the first draw stays bound, and the uniform staged for the second draw is PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE (psh.c:3793 reads the live register every draw). The A8R8G8B8 draw therefore runs with srcAlpha=ONE/dstAlpha=ZERO/ADD forced, and result.a is the combiner alpha instead of As*Fs + Ad*Fd -- wrong on a format whose alpha channel is real data and is read back as a texture. Run the transition the other way and the X8R8G8B8_Z draw stamps while the inherited pipeline still names SRC_ALPHA, so the colour blend consumes the stamped constant: arm 1's measured defect, reintroduced. This is the same hole the pre-existing destination-alpha fold already sits in -- the comment at draw.c:1807-1814 claims keying on the effective register fixes it, and that claim was already only true of the paths that rebuild the key -- but #59 widens the consequence from two blend factors to the whole alpha equation plus a SRC1 substitution, and one direction of it is the exact regression the change exists to prevent.
remediation: Give the colour surface format a generation counter, so the existing dirty check can see it: bump pg->pipeline_state_gen in DEF_METHOD(NV097, SET_SURFACE_FORMAT) when pg->surface_shape.color_format changes, exactly as the zeta arm three lines below already does for shader_state_gen. That is the cheapest fix, it repairs the pre-existing destination-alpha hole at the same time, and it is verifiable without a device. The alternative -- adding the guest colour format to RenderPassState -- is wrong, because it would split render passes that share a host format for no host reason. Reject any remediation that only widens the early-out's condition list without a counter: the early-out is reached from two places (draw.c:1730 check_pipeline_dirty and draw.c:1869) and a condition added to one of them leaves the other. PASS 2 SHOULD CHECK that the counter is bumped on the COLOR arm specifically and not folded into the zeta comparison, and that an A8R8G8B8 -> X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 transition at one address now reaches init_pipeline_key.
evidence: draw.c:1869-1881 (the early return, before any key is built), draw.c:1730-1772 (check_pipeline_dirty, gated on the same generations), draw.c:1774-1815 (init_pipeline_key, where the effective register enters), draw.c:1807-1814 (the comment whose claim this falsifies). pgraph.c:2461-2488 (SET_SURFACE_FORMAT: color_format assigned at 2465 with no generation bump; zeta bumps three counters at 2470-2474). pgraph.h:458-478 (generations are bumped only from pgraph_reg_w, and color_format is not a register). draw.c:1312-1317 (render-pass state carries only the host VkFormat). vk/surface.c:1810-1826 (bind_surface, the only pipeline_state_dirty setter on the surface path) and vk/surface.c:3298-3342 (the compatible-reuse path, which refreshes drawn_format/fmt/host_fmt and does not rebind). The eds3 path is NOT affected -- draw.c:4469-4472 recomputes the effective register every draw and compares it against r->dyn_state.blend, and draw.c:5403 / 5916 do the same for the reorder path; the comment at draw.c:4466-4468 states eds3 blend is supported on the Adreno part, which is why no arm on this fleet could see this.

summary: The withdrawal of #48's read-side swizzle is unconditional within the feature, but the write-side stamp that replaces it is not. surface_sampled_pad_alpha() returns VK_COMPONENT_SWIZZLE_IDENTITY for every pad-format surface once the gate is true, so a sampled pad alpha is now whatever byte the host image happens to hold. The stamp only writes that byte where the RASTER drew with alpha writes enabled. Three ordinary paths put non-stamped bytes into a colour surface image: a surface upload from guest RAM, an NV062 image blit whose destination bytes are patched in guest memory rather than in the image (vk/blit.c:513-557), and any draw with NV_PGRAPH_CONTROL_0_ALPHA_WRITE_ENABLE clear, where the forced alpha equation computes the stamp and the write mask discards it. On those pixels the sampled alpha regresses from the format's measured constant to a stale or guest-supplied byte. The lane's own text states the qualifier and then drops it: psh.h:180 says #48's approximation is 'exact on every pixel the raster drew'.
scenario: A title renders into X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8, then masks alpha writes off (D3DRS_COLORWRITEENABLE without the alpha channel) for a second pass over part of the surface, then samples the surface as a texture. Before this change the sampled alpha over the whole surface was 0, the measured hardware readback for a _Z format. After it, the masked region returns whatever the image held -- the previous pass's stamp if there was one, the uploaded guest byte if the region came from CPU writes, undefined if neither. The same applies to a scratch render target partly filled by an image blit: the blit patches guest memory (alpha_override 0xff for NV062 X8R8G8B8, 0 for X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8) and the host image's alpha for those pixels arrives through the upload path, not the raster. Blast radius is bounded -- only the four X-format surfaces, only when sampled as a texture, only on pixels the raster did not stamp -- which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH; but it is a behaviour regression against shipped code, and the stated reason for taking it is a MEASUREMENT one ('leaving it in would make the write side INVISIBLE'), which is a reason to run the arm with the swizzle out, not by itself a reason to fold with it out.
remediation: Two acceptable shapes, and the lane should pick rather than be told. (a) Keep the withdrawal and make the stamp cover the paths the swizzle used to: patch the pad byte on the surface UPLOAD path for pad formats, the way vk/blit.c already does for its own two NV062 formats, so every pixel in the image carries the constant however it got there. (b) Keep the swizzle for the 8888 pad formats, where the comment states the two corrections agree to the bit, and withdraw it only for the 1555 formats, where it is actively wrong (a 1555 surface sampled through an 8888 view reads two words as one texel). (b) is smaller and loses the 8888 half of the arm's visibility; (a) is the correct end state. Either way, say in the code what happens to a pad-format pixel the raster never wrote -- that sentence is what is missing, and its absence is what makes this look settled.
evidence: texture.c:1330-1368 (surface_sampled_pad_alpha, with the withdrawal at 1362). psh.h:180 ('exact on every pixel the raster drew'). vk/blit.c:131-153 (patch_alpha) and 513-557 (the NV062 per-format alpha_override: X8R8G8B8 -> 0xff, X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 -> 0), which is independent corroboration that the pad constant is real and that this codebase already patches it on a non-raster path. draw.c:2101-2110 and 4505-4514 (the alpha write mask, applied after the blend). psh.c:205-211 names vk/constants.h's sampled_pad_alpha column as the readback half that must stay in sync with the stamp.

summary: The registered prediction's arm B ref is not on the branch. b_ref is fab34eb3ea, which is NOT an ancestor of the branch tip 775389f537 -- merge-base --is-ancestor says no. Its patch-id is identical to 3519f4fc9e (both 7803c8d8c21a6dc28af5d4d79a24ed1ffae49717), so it is the same patch on an abandoned sha, reachable from the older branch origin/claude/padwrite59-dualsrc (tip c667750969). The dispatcher can therefore BUILD it successfully and silently produce an arm B that excludes the two commits after it: c3d4e121df (the nv2a index rebuild) and, critically, 775389f537 -- the commit that moves pgraph_glsl_set_dual_src_pad_supported() to after vkCreateDevice. The arm as bound measures the version with the gate set on the wrong side of device creation, which is the version the lane itself decided must not ship.
scenario: The hold is lifted and the queued request is claimed. The dispatcher resolves b_ref fab34eb3ea from origin/claude/padwrite59-dualsrc, builds, and the arm passes or fails against a tree that is not the fold candidate. If it passes, a verdict is recorded for code that will not be folded, and the fold then happens on unmeasured commits; if it fails, the failure is attributed to a mechanism the tip may already have changed. This is the failure mode MEMORY.md records as 'Ancestry asks about shas, not patches' and 'A stale baseline re-derives beautifully' -- and it does not announce itself, because the build succeeds. It is not hypothetical staleness either: 775389f537's own message says the earlier ordering left the renderer without a device while psh.c had already been told it may emit an Index decoration.
remediation: Re-register with b_ref set to the actual fold candidate (775389f537 at the time of writing, or whatever tip carries the remediations for H1-H3), and state in the prediction that fab34eb3ea and 3519f4fc9e are the same patch so the record of what was originally bound is not lost. a_ref 2445a6ff46 is fine -- it IS an ancestor of the tip and needs no change. Because H1-H3 will change the code before it folds, the re-registration should happen after those remediations land rather than now, so it is one action and not two. Do not fold the validity gate away while doing it: arm A must still read Clear/SFC_X1R5G5B5_Z1R5G5B5 = 49,152 and Blend_surface/*DstAlpha* = 0 on all 16, and that gate is the good part of this prediction.
evidence: docs/testing/predictions/issue59-dual-source-pad-write.json (a_ref 2445a6ff46, b_ref fab34eb3ea). merge-base --is-ancestor fab34eb3ea 775389f537 -> non-zero; merge-base --is-ancestor 2445a6ff46 775389f537 -> zero. patch-id --stable over fab34eb3ea and over 3519f4fc9e both give 7803c8d8c21a6dc28af5d4d79a24ed1ffae49717. branch -a --contains fab34eb3ea -> remotes/origin/claude/padwrite59-dualsrc only. The commits between fab34eb3ea and the tip are be84dc885f, c3d4e121df and 775389f537, plus the two re-committed source commits 924e5e7fc6 and 3519f4fc9e.

summary: The old query-only dualSrcBlend block is still compiled and still executes, immediately below the new one. It calls vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures a second time and prints a second line naming the same feature: 'Vulkan feature dualSrcBlend : available (query only, #59)', and on Android 'vk dualSrcBlend: available (query only, #59)'. The comment above it says it is kept 'because it is the derivation' -- but what was kept is the code, not just the prose, and the prose is the part with the value.
scenario: The prediction's own FAILS IF clause instructs the reader to read 'vk dualSrcBlend: enabled' in the logcat before believing a pass. A grep for `vk dualSrcBlend:` now returns two lines per boot, and on a part that reports the feature with maxFragmentDualSrcAttachments == 0 they say opposite things -- 'available but limit 0, NOT enabled' followed by 'available (query only, #59)'. The exact string the prediction names is still present when the feature is enabled, so the check does not break; but this line is the arm's only evidence that the write side came up at all, and the reason #59 stood blocked for a day is that nobody read this exact line. A log that prints two verdicts for one feature is the wrong instrument to hand that job to.
remediation: Delete the second block's CODE and keep its comment, moved above the new block or merged into it. If the derivation is worth preserving verbatim, preserving the comment does that; preserving a duplicate vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures call and a contradictory log line does not. If the lane prefers to keep both lines, change the old one's text so a grep can tell them apart, and say in the prediction which line is the evidence.
evidence: instance.c:987-1009 (the new block: the enable decision, the verdict string and the log line) and instance.c:1034-1045 (the old block, still live: a second vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures and a second log line). docs/testing/predictions/issue59-dual-source-pad-write.json, FAILS IF clause. docs/testing/nv2a_issues.toml [issue.59] blocker_tested, which records that the original line printed on thirty-eight runs across four lanes unread.

summary: pad_write_color_factor's SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE rationale is wrong in the direction it claims. The comment says 'A draw that combined SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE with a pad format would read the stamped constant, which is the arm-1 defect confined to one factor'. Work the arithmetic: for RGB the factor is min(As, 1 - Ad), and after this change As is the stamped constant and -- wherever the destination was itself stamped or cleared -- Ad is the same constant. For a _Z format that is min(0, 1) = 0; for an _O format min(1, 0) = 0. Hardware, with Ad = 1 on a format that stores no alpha, gives min(As, 0) = 0. So the patched behaviour AGREES with silicon on this factor, in both variants, rather than reproducing arm 1's defect.
scenario: No failure scenario -- this finding is about the reasoning, not the code, and the code is right, so it is an opinion and is downgraded accordingly. The residual gap is a different and narrower one than the comment names: an _O surface whose destination alpha came from somewhere other than the stamp or the clear (see M1) has Ad != 1, so min(1, 1-Ad) is not 0 and the result is wrong. That case is worth one sentence because it is the case M1's remediation also closes. Recorded because AGENTS.md's own note is that a wrong comment is not neutral -- audit pass 1's M3 was overstated on the strength of a stale sentence in this same file family.
remediation: Rewrite the paragraph to say what is true: SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE needs no substitution because under the stamp it already evaluates to the hardware answer for both pad variants, and the residual case is a pad-format destination whose alpha did not come from the raster or the clear. Leaving the factor alone stays correct; only the justification changes. No code change.
evidence: draw.c:592-635 (pad_write_color_factor and its comment, with the SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE paragraph at 612-623). draw.c:304-323 (blend_factor_with_dst_alpha_one, whose parallel decision to leave SATURATE alone is correctly justified as unmeasured rather than as defective). psh.h:145-149 (the constants stamped: 0.0 for _Z, 1.0 for _O). draw.c:288-302 (all four pad formats are in the dst-alpha-is-one set, which is what makes Ad = 1 the hardware answer here).

summary: padAlphaMode joins PSH_UNIFORM_DECL_X, and psh.c:2022-2024 emits every entry of PshUniformInfo unconditionally for both renderers, so the GL and GLES fragment shaders now carry an unused `uniform int padAlphaMode;`. Functionally harmless: the driver strips it, locs[PshUniform_padAlphaMode] comes back -1, and psh.c:3772 skips staging. Worth recording only because the GLES hazard this change is built around is stated as a claim about GL and GLES generating unchanged GLSL, and the generated GL shader text is in fact one line different from before the patch.
scenario: No failure scenario, so this is an opinion about tidiness and about how the claim will be read, and is downgraded accordingly. The claim that matters -- that neither `layout(location = 0, index = 1)` nor the stamp can reach a `#version 300 es` shader -- does hold, and holds for a structural reason: both sites are gated on ps->opts.vulkan as well as on the device flag, and psh_convert is the only place either string is emitted. The only consequence of the extra uniform is that a differ comparing generated GL GLSL against a pre-patch capture will show it.
remediation: Reviewed, not fixed, is an acceptable outcome here and is probably the right one -- keying a uniform declaration on the renderer would split the one macro that currently guarantees the shader text and the host-side offsets agree, which is a worse trade than an unused int. If it is left, log the decision, and do not describe the GL path as byte-identical to pre-patch in the fold note; describe it as unchanged in behaviour.
evidence: psh.h:201-209 (the DECL list with padAlphaMode at 204). psh.c:2022-2024 (`const char *u = ps->opts.vulkan ? "" : "uniform ";` then the unconditional loop over PshUniformInfo). glsl/common.h:55-89 (DECL_UNIFORM_TYPES: one macro drives the enum, the Values struct and the Info array, which is why splitting it is undesirable). psh.c:1998-2016 (frag_outputs: the non-Vulkan branch emits exactly the pre-patch string) and psh.c:3503 (the stamp, gated on ps->opts.vulkan).
